Cc: Don Proeschel <don.proeschel@utdallas.edu>
Subject: RE: How About a Fall Semester Marketing Project For Exos Aerospace?

Hello Edwin,

Thank you, Don, for the introduction. I would welcome a Fall semester marketing capstone team, and I think we can give your students an unusually good project.

Here is the short version of the client problem. Exos Aerospace is one of only three FAA-licensed reusable rocket launch providers in the United States. We have been flying suborbital vehicles since 2018, and our next flight of BLK3, our precision suborbital reusable launch vehicle, is targeted for early 2027 with roughly 135 kg of payload capacity still open to sell. The capstone challenge is to help us market and sell that payload space.

What makes this different from a normal marketing project is how the team would work. Exos runs an AI-native operating model we call EXO3, an internal fleet of AI agents that already handle research, outreach drafting, and CRM work. The capstone team would sit on top of that stack as the human strategy and creative layer, directing the agents rather than doing all the manual grind themselves. The students learn go-to-market marketing the modern way, humans setting strategy and creative while an agent fleet executes at scale, on a real revenue target. It is a strong story for the business school and, I would think, for your UTDesign showcase.

At a high level a semester could run like this:
- Weeks 1-2: onboard to the EXO3 stack and brand assets, define the ideal payload customer
- Weeks 3-5: segment and size the payload market (university research, defense and government test, in-space startups, sensor and component qualification, education and brand payloads)
- Weeks 5-8: build the campaign, a payload buyer microsite, one-pager, pitch deck, and a social and video series under our SPACEavailable campaign
- Weeks 8-12: run AI-augmented outreach, students author the messaging and creative and the agent fleet personalizes and scales it, all sends approved on our side
- Weeks 12-15: qualify the pipeline, advance the payload manifest for the 2027 flight, and deliver a final presentation and a reusable playbook

We would provide governed access to our tools, brand assets, media, and direct time with me and our BD team. I have put the full project scope in a short brief I can send along once we connect.

Would you have a team available for the fall, and do you have time for a short call this week or next to walk through it? Happy to work around your schedule.

Best regards,

John Quinn

title: APPROVAL - Reply to Jess Sponable (NFA) with LVES draft charter + template
question: Send this reply to Jess Sponable? On Yes, I deliver the ready-to-send draft (with the LVES charter draft attached) to YOUR inbox for you to send. It does not go to Jess directly.
context:
Jess asked (2026-08-20) for a draft charter / draft contents and a committee-charter template in the proper format. Draft charter built (drafts/LVES_Charter_DRAFT_v0.1_2026-08-20.md, attached to MC task 2169) in standard AIAA TC format, expanding the current LVES scope per Jess's takes (ELV+RLV, reusable upper stages/SM&L/ISAM/refueling, hypersonic suborbital in-core, hypersonic aircraft as interfaces, operability/reliability/safety cross-cutting). Reply answers both her questions and engages each scope point.

----- DRAFT REPLY -----
To: Jess Sponable <jess@nfaero.com>
Subject: RE: LVES Charter Working Group - Action

Hello Jess,

Good instincts on all of it, and yes, I have something concrete. I put together a first draft of the charter plus the contents we should include, and I built it in the standard AIAA TC format so it drops straight into the working group. Draft is attached.

On your two questions:

1. Draft charter / draft of contents: attached as a v0.1. It builds on the current LVES TC scope we already have and expands it along the lines you raised, rather than starting from a blank page.

2. Template in the proper format: because LVES is already an AIAA Technical Committee, the AIAA TC charter is the format, Committee Name, Scope, Governance, Roles and Responsibilities, with a versioned header and an annual review. If you want clean sister examples in that exact format, the AIAA Adaptive Structures and Transformational Flight charters are both public on aiaa.org, and the AIAA TAD Policy and Procedures points to a sample charter in the TC Chair Handbook. I patterned the draft on those.

On your scope takes, here is how I handled each in the draft:

- ELVs and RLVs: core, full vehicle systems and operations.
- Upper stages stepping to reusable upper stages: core, with SM&L, ISAM, refueling, and dynamic maneuver named as the enabling technologies, so we interface to that future without pretending we own the whole in-space architecture.
- Hypersonic suborbital rockets: in core, since they share vehicle, propulsion integration, GNC, thermal, and operations technology with launch and entry.
- Rocket-powered and airbreathing hypersonic aircraft: named as interfaces rather than absorbed. The common-technology argument is real, which is exactly why I kept them as coordinated interfaces, so we capture the shared tech without losing the constraint or stepping on the hypersonics committees.
- Operability, reliability, and safety of RLVs and ELVs: made a standing cross-cutting theme, since that is the connective tissue across every concept on the list.

I also added explicit exclusions, because constraining the problem matters as much as defining it, and one governance item: an objectives ledger baked into the charter from day one, every objective with an owner, a deliverable, a due date, and a quarterly status, so this committee produces named sessions and a roadmap rather than another round of minutes. Happy to stand that up and maintain it for the group.

Take a red pen to it. I would rather hand John Vinson a marked-up draft than more open discussion.

Best,
John

title: Approve the fix that makes Mission Control decisions readable and keeps your notes?
question: Should Exo apply the two-part fix (preserve notes + make every decision self-contained) to Mission Control?
context: You flagged on BD-032 that decisions arrive with no backstory and that notes you add don't reach the person getting the approval/denial. I traced both to real bugs:  (A) When anyone answers a decision, the code overwrites the note field — and blanks it if no new note is typed — so context notes are lost.  (B) The 'decision answered' alert only goes to the person waiting; when you are BOTH the assignee and the answerer (your case on BD-032), it skips entirely, so your note to John is never delivered.  Fix: notes are appended with who+timestamp and never erased; the answer+note is always routed to the requester; and every Exobot-generated decision must include plain-language Background, 'why this is your call', the actual ask, options-with-consequences, and links — acronyms spelled out. Full spec + a before/after rewrite of BD-032 is attached to Task #2489. Changes are small and reversible.

On Standard-only: ship just the legibility standard, hold the note-routing code change. On Hold: park it.
options: Approve — apply both fixes + the authoring standard

title: Send reply to Anselmo Pontes (Autogenetics) — GA/evolutionary trajectory-optimization brief
question: Approve sending this reply to Anselmo Pontes (Autogenetics) with the specific-problems write-up he requested, then a meeting in the next two weeks? Edit freely before sending.
context:
John reached out after Anselmo's HelioTech talk; Anselmo replied warmly (8/31, CC Neil Milburn) asking for a brief description of the specific trajectory problems before meeting. Draft reply below.

----- DRAFT (To: anselmo@autogenetics.ai; Cc: nmilburn@exosaero.com) -----
Subject: RE: Anselmo Pontes (Autogenetics) — evolutionary algorithms / trajectory convergence

Hello Anselmo,

Thank you, it was a genuine pleasure comparing notes, and I appreciate you offering to dig into the trajectory side with me. Here is the brief you asked for.

The core question I want your read on: do evolutionary/genetic methods converge more robustly, and toward better global optima, than the gradient-based approaches (direct collocation / pseudospectral transcription solved with SQP) we typically reach for on these problems? Ours are non-convex, heavily constrained, and often multi-objective, exactly the regime where gradient methods get pinned to a local optimum or stall on a poor initial guess.

The specific problems I have in mind, all on a reusable suborbital vehicle (our BLK3):

1. Powered-descent / propulsive-landing guidance. Converging on fuel-optimal descent-and-landing trajectories under thrust, thermal, and structural-load constraints, with tight terminal precision at the pad.

2. Ascent optimization. Pitch and throttle program to hit a target apogee/altitude with minimum propellant while staying inside our load limits (nominal boost under ~4g, transients to ~7g).

3. Coast and apogee targeting, plus contingency/abort trajectories off nominal.

Where I would most value your view: whether an evolutionary method, possibly hybridized with a local refinement step, converges more reliably across this set than what we use today, where you have seen it work well, and where it does not. If there is a fit, a natural extension is coupling the trajectory to vehicle-configuration/aero geometry, which is closer to the free-molecular-flow work you presented.

The easiest way to find a time in the next couple of weeks is to book directly on my calendar here, and I will hold Tuesdays and Thursdays open since those work best for you:
https://outlook.office365.us/bookwithme/user/3d1b68ea7e5643f9b2e76624f9dfd95f%40exosaero.com?anonymous&ismsaljsauthenabled

Best Regards,
John

title: Approve reply to Mike Chacos (TradeVector→PaceZero) — $750K BLK3 F2 advance: equity guarantee + creative structures
question: VERDICT: Reply is ready — confirms equity guarantee IS available and offers a 5-option menu that removes PaceZero's 'this is really a loan' objection. Approve to go out over your signature? (3 factual blanks for you to fill: TACFI match/timeline, what was represented re NASA IDIQ, Flight 1 remaining capacity.) context:
Mike Chacos (TradeVector) is shopping your $750K revenue-based advance to a new investor, PaceZero. His blocker: a clean receivable purchase can't carry the risk that Flight 2 doesn't sell out — that's a loan, which he won't do. He asked whether Exos equity is available as collateral (you said yes) and for demand data + answers on NASA IDIQ, TACFI, timing, and Flight 1 capacity.

The draft answers all of it and turns the equity guarantee into a menu that de-risks PaceZero (equity-collateralized advance / gov backstop sweep / convertible / receivable+warrant / first-loss reserve + Flight 3 oversell). Full draft below.

SECURITIES GATE: the reply only says equity collateral is *available* and floats structures — no binding terms. Before any equity-pledge/convertible terms are actually papered, route final structure to the securities approver + Marion Keyes.

----- DRAFT REPLY -----

# DRAFT reply — John → Mike Chacos (TradeVector), for PaceZero
**Re:** Exos Aerospace — $750K revenue-based advance against BLK3 Flight 2 payload receivables
**Date drafted:** 2026-09-09 · Awaiting John's approval (Decision on his matrix)
**Jon must fill 3 brackets before send:** TACFI match/timeline · what was represented re: NASA IDIQ · Flight 1 remaining capacity

---

Mike,

Good to reconnect — answers below, and yes, an equity guarantee is on the table. Let me lay out the structure options so you and PaceZero have room to get comfortable, then hit your specific questions.

**Equity guarantee + ways to structure the downside**

You're right that a clean receivable purchase can't carry the risk that we don't sell the Flight 2 bay — that's a loan, and I'm not asking you to write one. The point of collateral is to take that risk off PaceZero. Options, in order of how much they de-risk you:

1. **Equity-collateralized advance.** We pledge Exos equity (a share pledge and/or warrant coverage) as security. If the Flight 2 receivables haven't repaid the $750K plus carry by March 30, 2027, the shortfall converts to Exos equity at the Series A price rather than triggering a cash repurchase. PaceZero's downside is secured by equity value, not by our capacity fill.

2. **Government backstop as a senior repayment source.** Behind the bay sits a $4M DoD TACFI and a $2M Texas Space Commission grant now moving — an in-person presentation to the Commission by Senator Bob Hall's Chief of Staff last week, with multiple Congressional letters of support. We can assign approved proceeds to sweep to PaceZero first — a repayment source that doesn't depend on payload sales at all.

3. **Convertible note.** If a receivable sale can't hold the performance risk on your side, we do the $750K as a convertible into the Series A at a discount, with the Flight 2 deposits sweeping for accelerated cash return. Secured downside, Series A upside.

4. **Blended purchase + warrant kicker.** Buy the receivable at the agreed discount and attach warrants, so your return isn't tied only to how fast the bay fills.

5. **First-loss reserve + Flight 3 oversell right.** We fund a deposit reserve as first-loss and give you the Flight 3 oversell as a second collection window — two shots at repayment.

Mix and match — happy to paper whichever combination PaceZero is most comfortable with.

**Your questions**

- **Does capacity like this sell out?** Structurally, yes — NASA Flight Opportunities is a standing federal buyer of exactly this suborbital research capacity, and Blue Origin's New Shepard and Zero-G fly recurring, oversubscribed research manifests. Closer to home: entX signed the Flight 1 LSA and we've collected $400K+ against it — we sign, collect, and fly. Behind Flight 2 is a priced pipeline north of $100M / 350+ opportunities, worked daily by our EXO3 payload engine and the UTD team, booking now. I'll share the pipeline detail under NDA.

- **NASA IDIQ.** The NASA path we referenced is the Flight Opportunities on-ramp, which activates once BLK3 completes two flights above 85 km — not the Aug 17 IDIQ you found. Happy to walk through the distinction. *[JON — confirm exactly what was represented here so I frame it right.]*

- **TACFI process/timing.** *[JON — confirm match amount + award timeline.]* The mechanism requires a private/non-federal match, which is exactly where a $750K commitment does double duty: it funds Flight 2 and helps anchor the match that unlocks the larger award.

- **Timing / what the $750K does.** entX's $400K completes a portion, but full build + integration + fly for Flight 2 is ~$1.1M. The $750K is the bridge that gets the vehicle to its second launch, repaid from Flight 2 payload sales by March 30, 2027.

- **Flight 1 capacity.** *[JON — confirm remaining capacity on Flight 1 / whether entX filled it.]*

Easiest path is probably 15 minutes by phone this week to pick the structure PaceZero wants, then I'll get you a term summary to book. Let me know what works.

Best regards,

John

John Quinn
Cofounder and CEO
Exos Aerospace Systems & Technologies, Inc.

If total US need exceeds $10M/12mo, move the US raise to Reg D 506(b)/(c) — no dollar cap.

PATH B — FIEA private placement into the K.K. (the Japanese analog of Reg D 504): Japanese investors buy K.K. shares directly. Brings local capital + partners, does NOT touch your US 504 cap, keeps foreign equity at the sub so the US parent stays 100% US-owned (CFIUS-clean). FEFTA prior-notification applies to the US parent funding the aerospace K.K. This is the structure the 4 existing 'Japan Seed' decisions already detail (entity/share-class/custody/size) — they are Path-B mechanics, not the 504 question.

So: 504-to-fund-Japan is viable only by funding the K.K. from the US parent's single raise (Path A) — a standalone second 504 for Japan would breach the 12-month cap.

title: OILR/PAD $360K MMOU vs. self-leasing our own West Texas pad
question: You're right that we'd be funding the cheap half of the problem. Decline PAD's $360K cost-share and pursue a self-leased far-West-TX pad instead (keeping PAD only as a zero-dollar anchor-operator MOU + Lourcey → Series A)? Pick the path.
context:
YOUR READ IS CORRECT — and it holds up under the numbers. The land is NOT the scarce or expensive input; the FAA Part 450 site qualification + the independent §450.145 highly-reliable Flight Safety System (FSS) is. And Exos pays that qualification cost IDENTICALLY whether the pad sits on PAD's site or on land Exos leases itself. So PAD's $360K buys land access Exos can get for a small fraction — while Exos still funds 100% of the qualification burden regardless. That is paying twice for the cheap half of the problem.

WHAT THE $360K ACTUALLY IS (from Oscar's 9/22 MMOU, reviewed for Neil — Task 2451): roughly one-third of the revenue from a future full-manifest second BLK3 mission, handed to PAD to fund THEIR site's qualification. That inverts the value exchange. Exos is the scarce asset here — a 1-of-3 FAA-licensed reusable operator whose engagement is the only thing that gives PAD's raw acreage FAA site-eval priority, plus a booked BLK3 mission that IS the revenue engine. The anchor operator does not also write the check to qualify the developer's dirt. Site feasibility / flight-safety / the FAA site-add are the site developer's burden — exactly what TSC grant money ($500K SEARF) + Aerospace Corp are funding on the Concho Valley play. PAD should fund its site from Lourcey's capital or a grant, not from Exos mission revenue.

SELF-LEASE ECONOMICS (far West Texas / Trans-Pecos): the real requirement is not a 30-ft pad — it's the remote overflight/exclusion GEOMETRY and low population density around it (your “30+ mi from an Interstate” instinct is exactly the range-safety buffer). That is abundant and cheap out there. A surface-use / launch-hazard lease over a section + buffer is order-of-magnitude tens of thousands/yr (grazing land runs low single-digit-to-$15/ac/yr; a launch-day hazard easement adds a premium) vs. $360K one-time to PAD — and Exos keeps full control of site, timeline, and terms and gives away NO exclusivity. Blue Origin's Van Horn private-land, minimal-infra VTVL site is the precedent: remote desert scrub, private land, suborbital VTVL.

ROOT CAUSE: cron/subagent completions that announce INTO a Discord channel route through that channel's interactive agent session and wake an agent turn; when that wake hangs on the claude-cli backend (120s gateway timeout) the run is left stuck-active and clogs the SHARED guild-channel path, so every guild channel stops creating turns (DMs use a separate path, unaffected). ~14 crons announce into channels (7 stacked on #rd-team; the 11:00 Investor cron triggered today's 11:09 freeze).

Digests land in the same channels; the wedge can't form. Requires creating 1 Discord webhook per channel + editing ~14 cron jobs. Blast radius: if a webhook URL is wrong a digest silently stops landing, so I'd convert one channel at a time and verify.

Secondary hygiene (low risk, can bundle): stagger the 7 #rd-team crons; remove stale openclaw installs (24.14/24.15) and repoint Mission Control (node 24.14/v2026.6.35) to 24.21 so no old-client calls hit the newer gateway.

title: Employment Agreement: define severance, or keep case by case?
question: Sec. 6(A) of the Employment Agreement puts conditions on severance the agreement never defines. Which way do you want the new-hire template to go?
context:
WHAT: The Employment Agreement (the version Victor signed 7/30/2026 and every employee on that form) says in Sec. 6(A) that "subsections (b) and (c) below" pay out only after the employee signs a general release. But 6(B) and 6(C) are just definitions ("Cause" and "Permanent Disability"). The agreement never says what severance anyone gets: no amount, no formula, no trigger. So the release condition has nothing to attach to, and "Cause" is defined but never used for anything.

WHAT'S ALREADY FIXED (9/28, commit e99878d): the release can no longer block reporting to the government. New-hire template EXOS_Employment_Agreement_Template_Rev_2026-09-28.docx; new standard Separation Agreement & General Release (protected-activity carve-out, age-discrimination waiver rules, federal labor-law-safe confidentiality); Attachment A Sec. 6.5 covers current staff through the 11/1 signature. The template currently reads "no severance pay or other termination benefit the Company MAY OFFER ... unless you sign the release," which works whether or not severance exists.

THE CHOICE:
(1) Case by case (current template): no promised severance. Exos offers a package only when it wants a release, sized to the situation. Maximum flexibility and no liability on the books. Downside: weaker recruiting pitch, and every separation is a one-off negotiation.
(2) Standard formula: e.g. X weeks of base pay per year of service (min/max), paid only on termination without Cause (or for Permanent Disability) and only after a signed release. This gives Cause and Permanent Disability a real job. It's predictable and helps recruiting senior engineers, but creates a contingent liability to disclose in Series A diligence. Tell me the formula and I'll draft it.
(3) Tiered by role: severance only for officers/key hires, written into their individual offer letters; the standard template stays case by case.

ALSO OPEN: the template keeps the original optional [bracketed] clauses (outside boards, annual salary review, sales comp, background check, indemnification/D&O). Each should be kept or deleted before the next new-hire signing. I can do that in the same pass.

Recommendation: (1) now, while the Series A is live and headcount is ~13. Add individual severance for key hires only when needed, which is effectively (3). Revisit a formula after the raise closes.
proposedAction: On your answer I update EXOS_Employment_Agreement_Template_Rev_2026-09-28.docx (and resolve the [bracketed] clauses if you say so), rebuild the PDF, and log it on task #3227. Existing signed agreements are unchanged. Any change for current staff would need a signed amendment.
options: Key hires only, in offer letters

title: AEDC Velocity: bid the Test Facility Scanning & 3D Modeling project?
question: Pursue the AEDC facility scanning/3D modeling opportunity?
context:
AEDC Velocity Alliance project: 'AEDC Test Facility Scanning and High-Definition 3D Modeling' (SOO, Jon forwarded 10/4).
SCOPE: laser-scan + as-built models of AEDC test facilities. FY27 Phase 1 = VKF Yard+Plant (~1.04M scan sq ft). Out-years ~17.5M more sq ft (PWT, ETF, ASTF, J5/J6, APTU...) = 18.5M total, 5-yr multi-phase. Deliverables: ±1/4 in accuracy (1/8 favored), LOD 350 (400 favored) Revit models, intelligent Autodesk Plant 3D process model tied to AEDC P&IDs, DWG sets, ReCap/E57 point clouds, Navisworks, QC deviation reports, training + support. ALL data = CUI (NIST 800-171), CONUS, U.S. citizens only, CAC/DBIDS base access, 3rd-shift/weekend work around test schedule, AEDC approval for every scanner/drone/camera.

FIT: Exos has NO scan-to-BIM capability (no scanners, Revit/Plant 3D modelers or survey staff). This is an A-E / reality-capture job, not launch/test work. Exos could only prime it as integrator: PM/IMS, QC, CUI enclave (GCC High), and process/pressure-system engineering review of the Plant 3D model (our cryo/pressure-system background). A specialized scan-to-BIM firm would do ~80-90% of the work.

FOR bidding: (1) first funded AEDC task under Velocity = past performance + day-to-day presence inside AEDC test facilities, ahead of the hypersonic/flight-test work we actually want there; (2) multi-year follow-on volume; (3) fits the consortium-prime model.
AGAINST: (1) pulls PM bandwidth off the BLK3 + HVRR standing focus; (2) a pass-through prime is weak on 'significant extent' + evaluators will see it; (3) CUI/NIST 800-171 posture must be provable (SPRS score not yet posted; Lizi's ECA cert still pending); (4) long on-site 3rd-shift work in Tullahoma TN, far from Greenville; (5) FFP risk on out-years.

RECOMMENDATION: CONDITIONAL GO as prime ONLY if, within ~7 days, we sign a teaming partner that (a) has done DoD/industrial-plant scan-to-BIM at LOD 350 + Plant 3D, (b) has U.S.-citizen crews and its own NIST 800-171/CMMC + JCP, (c) prices its scope FFP. Exos role = prime/PM/QC/CUI + process-model engineering. If no qualified partner in 7 days -> PASS (or support that partner as a sub if they want to prime). Due date is NOT in the SOO -> Exo to pull it from the Velocity call/announcement before anything else.
proposedAction: Pull due date; shortlist + contact 3-5 scan-to-BIM firms w/ DoD/industrial Plant 3D work; teaming MNDA; go/no-go on day 7

title: NASA STRI26 RDRE institute (released today): join a university team as industry partner?
question: NASA released the RDRE Space Technology Research Institute on NSPIRES today. It has to be university-led, and industry can only join as a partner. Do we go after a teaming slot before pre-proposals close on 11/3?
context:
Source: NSPIRES NNH26ZTR001N-26STRI_B3, Appendix B3 (released 10/5/2026): https://nspires.nasaprs.com/external/solicitations/summary!init.do?solId={2E039405-794F-19D8-24ED-386F15C3C77A}&path=open

KEY TERMS
- Topic: Enabling Future RDRE Design Capabilities. NASA's main interest is 5-165 klbf LOX/hydrocarbon engines, with LOX/methane emphasized. The headline goal is to design, build and test at least one thrust chamber assembly that gets 3% or more specific impulse over a comparable conventional engine. It runs in 3 phases: loss mechanisms, then models, then TCA demo.
- Funding: one award as a grant, up to $13M over 5 years and no more than $3.25M in any year. $4M is available now. Target award date is May 2027.
- Who can lead: the PI must be a faculty member at the lead university, and each PI can lead only one proposal. At least 3 US universities are required, each getting 15% or more of the budget. At least 70% of the budget must go to universities, so industry plus nonprofits share 30% at most.
- NASA Centers, including MSFC, are NOT allowed to collaborate on proposals. NASA civil servants can't be on teams. That means Dankanich and Teasley can't be on our team or help write the proposal. Technical questions go only to hq-stmd-stri@mail.nasa.gov and the public FAQ.
- Dates: town hall 10/15 1-2pm ET. Mandatory pre-proposal 11/3 (5-page technical plan plus summary chart, dual-anonymous review). Full proposal 1/21/2027.

HOW EXOS FITS (staying inside our guardrails): we'd be an industry subawardee to a lead university doing TCA fabrication and integration support, plus a path to fly on our reusable suborbital platform after the institute. We would NOT be named as an RDRE developer or propulsion provider. It runs in parallel with the $2.5M Phase III sole-source ask and doesn't replace it.

title: DD CAUTION: Harry Topham / Resonance (Space Insider). Legit vendor sales pitch, low value
question: Verdict: CAUTION. This is a real company, but the email is a sales pitch for a paid market-intel subscription, not an opportunity. Recommend no reply, or at most a 20-min call to take the free insights. Which?
context:
Inbound 10/8 08:03 to jquinn@, subject 'exos - upcoming launch demand'. The offer: an intro call with 'live insights on upcoming missions and operators relevant to EXOS'.
Findings:
- Resonance Alliance Inc. is real. It's a Toronto vertical-intelligence firm founded 2019 that runs The Quantum Insider, AI Insider and Space Insider; LinkedIn shows ~49 staff, Evan Kubes is President (https://resonance.holdings, https://thequantuminsider.com/about, https://uk.linkedin.com/company/resonance-holdings).
- Harry Topham is real: London-based Senior Associate on the Space Insider team page, described as 'driving business development for the platform' (https://spaceinsider.tech/company). His LinkedIn shows him in BD/sales since May 2025 (Huq Industries before that) and non-space roles before 2023 (https://linkedin.com/in/harry-topham). He is a sales rep, not an analyst.
- The pitch is a templated cold sequence. The free 'live insights' call is a demo hook for a paid data-platform subscription or advisory engagement. Resonance also sells paid 'enterprise marketing' (sponsored coverage).
- I couldn't verify the claim that they support organisations 'like Boeing'.
- Not a scam or advance-fee play, so it's not added to the failed-DD registry. DD dossier logged at /dossier.html.
Value to Exos: low. We already track launch demand in-house (BLK3 payload sales, past-customer list, BD capture). The only upside is a free market read, or later a paid sponsored-article channel.
proposedAction: No reply (default). If you want the free read, take a 20-min call, share no pipeline/customer data, and buy nothing.

question: Exo did all the verification. One action left: send this 4-paragraph email to Dr. Hartwig yourself (NASA = gov, so it comes from you). Recommendation: SEND NOW. It costs nothing and plants BLK3 Flight 2 (early 2027) with NASA's lead CFM researcher.

• Hook: NASA's own project record says no steady-state microgravity cryogenic flow-boiling data exists (https://techport.nasa.gov/projects/106638). His tests have flown on parabolic aircraft, which give about 15-20 s of low gravity. BLK3 gives about 150 s.

Best regards,
John Quinn
Cofounder and CEO, Exos Aerospace Systems & Technologies, Inc.

title: Approve SEC-CUI-XFER — CUI/ITAR/EAR Controlled Document Transfer Procedure
question: Approve SEC-CUI-XFER controlled document transfer procedure?
context:
Procedure SEC-CUI-XFER (DRAFT, Rev 0, 2026-10-09) was authored per your 10/9 request: "I need a way to transfer ITAR/EAR-sensitive documents in support of our ITAR/EAR process."

It is the companion to SEC-CUI-STOR (storage). It covers:
• Pre-transfer export gate (classify, CSL screen, export auth, need-to-know, NDA, CEO sign-off)
• Transfer methods: internal staff (SharePoint GCC High named permission) | U.S. partner/customer (GCC High external share, named+expiry+no-download) | U.S. Government (DoD SAFE, recipient-initiated) | Foreign person (STOP — license/TAA required) | Physical media (exception only)
• Marking requirements (CUI banner, ITAR/EAR export warning)
• Transfer log fields; ITAR 5-yr retention (22 CFR 122.5) and EAR 5-yr retention (15 CFR Part 762)
• Prohibited methods: email, Discord, chat, MC, personal cloud, AI tools/Exo
• Spillage/unauthorized disclosure: ITAR voluntary disclosure (22 CFR 127.12) and EAR VSD (15 CFR 764.5)
• GCC High tenant setup checklist (one-time, for Atomus/tenant admin)

File: process-library/08-security-cui/SEC-CUI-XFER_CUI_-_ITAR_-_EAR_Controlled_Document_Transfer_(Internal,_Partner,_Government).docx

How to transfer a controlled document TODAY (5-line summary):
1. GATE: Classify doc (ITAR/USML, EAR/ECCN, or CUI), screen recipient on CSL (https://www.trade.gov/consolidated-screening-list), confirm export auth (license/exemption/NLR), need-to-know, CUI NDA on file, and CEO sign-off.
2. INTERNAL STAFF: SharePoint GCC High → grant named-person permission on the specific file. No 'anyone' links. Notify via Teams/GCC High only.
3. U.S. PARTNER/CUSTOMER: SharePoint GCC High external share → specific named authenticated individuals only, 30-day expiry, download blocked. Send link via GCC High email or Teams only.
4. U.S. GOVERNMENT: Ask the Gov POC for a DoD SAFE drop-off link (https://safe.apps.mil). Upload from GCC High; delete local copy immediately after upload.
5. FOREIGN PERSON: STOP — no transfer without an approved ITAR license/TAA or EAR license. Escalate to CEO + legal immediately.
proposedAction: Approve procedure SEC-CUI-XFER Rev 0 as the Exos standard for controlled document transfer. Status will move from DRAFT to Approved.

title: FNEX: 6 protections if the PIPE funds but the RTO fails — add to the Advisory Agreement?
question: Recommended (all six): (1) Get FNEX's written acceptance of the bracketed PIPE NOTE/ESCROW and NET CLOSING CASH clauses. They are still in brackets in the 10/6 Board Copy, and without them a failed deal could leave Exos holding a note. (2) Failed-deal conversion: if Exos elects to convert escrowed PIPE money into Exos stock, it converts at no less than the last round ($14.00/sh), and it is NOT an 'FNEX-Introduced Investment' or Tail-fee event (otherwise 5% cash = ~$750K on $15M). (3) Escrow agent is an independent bank, never FNEX/Ainigma; Exos never takes possession before Closing. (4) Redefine 'Closing' as merger consummation PLUS Nasdaq approval of the initial-listing application (Rule 5110(a)), so fees aren't earned on a merger that then can't list. (5) PIPE investor list is pre-cleared before funding: restricted-party screening, plus a CFIUS/ITAR review by Counsel of any foreign investor, since conversion would put foreign holders in Exos equity. (6) Counsel confirms the note's exemption (Rule 506) and how it integrates with our open Rule 504 Series A (Rule 152), so a failed PIPE can't taint the 504 raise.
context: From the 10/6 MASTER Board Copy: fees are earned only at Closing, which means merger consummation; PIPE funding is not Closing. Escrow until Closing; Outside Date = 6 mo; on failure, proceeds are returned or, at Exos's option, convert to Exos common; no cash repayment ever; note is unsecured. Breakup fee only if Exos walks to a competing deal within 6 mo (greater of accrued $60K/mo or 0.5%, capped). 12-month Tail on Introduced Parties, plus non-circumvention. Exos's own risks that the agreement doesn't cover: PCAOB audit, Counsel and listing-prep spend; 6 months of management time; the Series A paused; reputational hit if the Target's 8-K makes the deal public.

title: FNEX PIPE: restructure escrow so SSLC closes FIRST, then the RTO (two-tranche PIPE)
question: The 10/6 Board Copy holds ALL PIPE proceeds in escrow until RTO Closing, which blocks your SSLC-first sequencing. Recommended structure: (1) Tranche A = the amount sized to the SSLC acquisition, released from escrow at the SSLC closing. • Best way to pay in yen: Wise Business. $31 one-time setup, mid-market FX, fees from 0.23% (https://wise.com/us/pricing/business). It pays JPY to a domestic Japanese bank account, usually about 1 working day after conversion (https://wise.com/help/articles/2932156/guide-to-jpy-transfers). Backup: BambooHR/Remote. Last resort: SWIFT wire.
What the procedure requires:
• Before any payment: a signed contractor agreement, a W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E, an OFAC/CSL screen, and an export check if technical data is shared (you as Empowered Official, with Denise reviewing).
• A monthly invoice in JPY with expenses and receipts on the same invoice. The contractor declares any days worked in the US, which triggers a 30% withholding review and a 1042-S. Work done entirely in Japan needs no 1099.
• Manager approval in MC. Finance prepares the Wise transfer and a second person releases it.
• Books record the USD actually debited, with the JPY amount in the memo. Employees with yen expenses use the new MC Expenses yen option (live, commit 7cd1514).
Two decisions come before first use: Kyle opens the Wise account, and the CPA decides whether to enable QBO Multicurrency. It can't be turned off and doesn't work with QBO Bill Pay (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/multicurrency/learn-multicurrency-quickbooks-online/L5krkKQi8_US_en_US).

title: Release Exo's Orbital Clarity briefing to the 6 UTD students?
question: John forwarded NASA's Orbital Clarity Challenge (register by Oct 28, 5 PM ET; up to $500K per winner; the FAQ says prize funds can be used however winners see fit). He asked Exo to brief Team Atlas, with you approving. Six emails, one per student, from Exo, cc you, Reply-To you. Each explains the prize and assigns one 20-min session (#3854, due Tue 10/20): flag which of their lead cards fit (upper-atmosphere/space-environment sensor builders). Students contact nobody; you pick who gets an invitation. Full text is in Context. Release them?
context:
Hi Roel,

John Quinn forwarded a NASA prize that could matter to some of the payload customers in your pipeline, and he asked me to brief the team on it.

WHAT IT IS
The NASA TechLeap Prize "Orbital Clarity Challenge." NASA wants low-cost sensors that can be built in quantity to measure atmospheric density, pressure, or drag in low Earth orbit. Up to four winners can each receive up to $500,000 over three phases ($200K, then $200K, then $100K). NASA also intends to give the final winners a test flight in orbit at no cost.
Key dates: registration closes Oct 28 at 5:00 PM ET. Phase 1 submissions close Nov 11 at 5:00 PM ET.
Sources: https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/stmd/prizes-challenges-crowdsourcing-program/nasa-techleap-prize-orbital-clarity-challenge
and https://occ.nasatechleap.org/awards/

WHY IT MATTERS TO OUR CUSTOMERS
The challenge FAQ says prize funds "can be used however the winners see fit" (https://occ.nasatechleap.org/frequently-asked-questions/). So a customer who wins could use part of the money to fund their experiment. One example is a recoverable BLK3 flight to test their sensor and get the hardware back before NASA's orbital test. John's idea is to invite the customers who fit, as a favor to them.
To be clear about what this is not: Exos isn't entering the challenge, and BLK3 isn't the orbital test flight NASA provides. If you describe it, say "a NASA prize that might fund your experiment." Don't say it's an Exos program.

WHO FITS
Only groups that build, or could build, sensors for the upper atmosphere or the space environment: atmospheric and space-physics labs, instrument makers, and small-satellite sensor companies. Most of our pipeline won't fit, and that's fine.

YOUR 20-MINUTE SESSION: task #3854, due Tue 10/20
Go through your own lead cards and post one note on #3854:
   FIT: organization | what they build that measures the upper atmosphere or space environment | link | lead card #
or: NONE from my cards
Roel checks that all six notes are in on Tuesday. The deadline is tight because invitations have to reach customers before NASA's Oct 28 registration cutoff.

As always, nobody on the team contacts a customer. Lizi decides who gets an invitation and sends it. If anything is unclear, post a question on #3854 and I'll answer there.

Talk soon,
Exo
Exos Aerospace · Mission Control
proposedAction: On Yes, Exo emails all 6 students (cc lquinn@exosaero.com, Reply-To you) within ~10 minutes. On No, nothing is sent; add a note with your edits and Exo revises and re-files.
